Net Income vs Free Cash Flow vs Owner FCF
charts.annotation: Owner FCF, where shown, is the DCF's series after SBC, interest income and lease principal.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For InnoCare Pharma Limited (諷誠健華): equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For InnoCare Pharma Limited (諷誠健華): the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For InnoCare Pharma Limited (諷誠健華): read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For InnoCare Pharma Limited (諷誠健華): the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For InnoCare Pharma Limited (諷誠健華): the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For InnoCare Pharma Limited (諷誠健華): the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For InnoCare Pharma Limited (諷誠健華): CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For InnoCare Pharma Limited (諷誠健華): the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For InnoCare Pharma Limited (諷誠健華): the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

revenueMix.title: Revenue composition: drug sales vs licensing/collaboration
revenueMix.content:
Drug sales is recurring China commercial revenue from orelabrutinib (across four NRDL-reimbursed indications) and, from Q4 2025, tafasitamab. Collaboration/licensing revenue is upfront payments and milestones from out-licensing deals -- chiefly Zenas BioPharma (ex-Greater China/SEA rights to orelabrutinib-in-MS and two preclinical autoimmune assets) and Prolium Bioscience (the CD20xCD3 bispecific ICP-B02).

For InnoCare Pharma Limited (諷誠健華): FY2025's jump to profitability and the headline revenue growth are driven largely by one-time deal income, not just commercial execution -- FY2025 drug sales grew 43.4% YoY (RMB1,005.6m to RMB1,442.4m) while collaboration revenue jumped from RMB3.8m to RMB932.5m on the Zenas and Prolium signings. H1 FY2026 shows the recurring line still compounding (drug sales +43.2% YoY to RMB918.1m) even as collaboration revenue normalizes lower than the FY2025 deal-signing spike.

What to watch:

  • Drug sales growth rate on its own -- this is the sustainable part of the story
  • Collaboration revenue reverting toward royalty-only run-rate once upfronts are recognized
  • New licensing deals or milestone triggers that would re-inflate this line without changing the commercial trajectory

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For InnoCare Pharma Limited (諷誠健華): the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
